Live camera in the demo, and the project moves to the MIT license.

**Live demo:** https://miguelmochizuki.github.io/fer-2013/

## Changes

- **Live camera.** "Use your camera" mirrors your video and classifies every face in it, continuously. Faces keep their number between frames and their readings are smoothed so they do not flicker; click a box or a crop to see one face's full reading and heatmap. Nothing leaves the tab. Measured in Chromium on a desktop with one WASM thread: about 7 analyses per second with one face, 4 with three, 3 with five.
- **MIT license** from this release on. v0.1.0 and v0.1.1 were published under the AGPL-3.0 and stay under it. The reason for the AGPL (a possible YOLO detector) is gone: the detector is YuNet, which is MIT.
- **Safer worker protocol.** Each analysis request carries an id and the worker runs them one at a time, so a photo chosen while the camera is on can no longer receive a camera frame's result.

## Unchanged

The model is `models-v1.2.0` (int8), the API and its Docker image are as in v0.1.1.

## Known limits

- About 71% accuracy on a noisy dataset, measured on acted 48x48 faces: a webcam in poor light or at an angle will be read worse. Emotion labels read off a face are not reliable. Do not use this for decisions about people.
- Small faces in a large photo can be missed, because detection runs on the image downscaled to 640 px.
- PNGs with transparency reach the model as black where alpha is 0.
- The demo is checked in Chromium and Firefox (photos); the camera mode was tested in Chromium with a synthetic video stream. Safari is untested.
